newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden should join ERM - Riksbank's Feldt.
newsitem.headline: Sweden should join ERM - Riksbank's Feldt.

text.p: Kjell-Olof Feldt, Chairman of the governing board of Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Monday Sweden should link the crown to the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).

"I believe an ERM entry is natural given the financial stability that is beginning emerge in Sweden. Some time or other we have to decide which currency policy we are going to follow," Feldt told business magazine Veckans Affarer.

Feldt, a former finance minister and a respected voice in the ruling Social Democratic Party, called on the government to play a more active role in the heated debate surrounding Swedish memberhsip of the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"The government is too passive on the EMU issue. Those in cabinet who believe Sweden should join EMU should attempt to lead the debate," he said.

He said the government was taking too long in formulating its ERM and EMU strategy by waiting for an official report on membership of ERM -- due to be unveiled next Monday -- and for the EU's Dublin summit in December.
Prime Minister Goran Persson has said the Social Democratic Party leadership will make a recommendation to the party congress next September on ERM and EMU.
But Feldt said Persson and Finance Minister Erik Asbrink should make their own views known straight away.
"If they are in favour, they should say so, if not, they should also say so. For many people, their final view will be dictated by the opinion of leading politicians," said Feldt.
"There's not much point in calling for a free and open debate if you don't take part in it yourself," he added.
